vulnerability.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
vulnerability.description: Vulnerabilities that allow attackers to induce the server to make requests
vulnerability.impact: Access to internal services, data theft, or system compromise via internal network
vulnerability.mitigation: Validate and sanitize URLs, use allowlists, block private IPs and local hostnames

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability
findings.explanation: The contract allows a user to initiate an external call, which can be exploited for Server-Side Request Forgery.
findings.impact: Potential access to internal services or data theft via the Solidity smart contract
exploitation_steps: Replace the external contract with an attacker-controlled contract
findings.exploitation_conditions: An attacker needs to have Ethereum to execute transactions and must be able to interact with the smart contract
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitize URLs used in external calls, use allowlists, block private IPs and local hostnames

chunk_analyses.notes: This Solidity smart contract demonstrates a Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability when interacting with external contracts.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability found
findings.explanation: The function 'airDrop' allows user input to call the 'supportsToken' function, which can be manipulated to perform SSRF attacks.
findings.impact: Potential data theft or access to internal services via SSRF.
findings.execution_path_diagram:
```
	+---> airDrop (caller input)
	   |                 |
	   |                 | supportsToken
	   v                 v|
	   Bank.supportsToken() (user-controlled argument) ---- SSRF vulnerability ---
```
exploitation_steps: Call 'airDrop' function with a crafted URL as an argument to 'supportsToken'
Exploit SSRF vulnerability in the Bank.supportsToken() call
findings.exploitation_conditions: Attacker has the ability to call 'airDrop' function.
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitize all URL inputs and use allowlists.

chunk_analyses.notes: Check other functions for potential SSRF vulnerabilities.
